vodka.definition: A distilled alcoholic spirit usually presented as clear and relatively neutral in character.
vodka.exampleUsage: The stock record identifies the closed bottle as vodka.

gin.definition: A distilled alcoholic spirit flavored mainly with juniper berries.
gin.exampleUsage: The catalogue describes the gin’s juniper character.

rum.definition: A distilled alcoholic spirit made from fermented sugarcane products.
rum.exampleUsage: The product record describes the rum as a sugarcane spirit.

tequila.definition: Mexican liquor made from fermented juices of an agave plant.
tequila.exampleUsage: The trainee checks the tequila’s declared origin.

whiskey.definition: A liquor made from fermented mash of grain.
whiskey.exampleUsage: The inventory separates whiskey from the fruit-based spirits.

bourbon.definition: Whiskey distilled from a mash of corn and malt and rye and aged in charred oak barrels.
bourbon.exampleUsage: The product sheet lists bourbon as a type of whiskey.

scotch.definition: Whisky produced in Scotland under the applicable product rules.
scotch.exampleUsage: The origin record identifies the Scotch as produced in Scotland.

brandy.definition: Distilled from wine or fermented fruit juice.
brandy.exampleUsage: The catalogue distinguishes brandy from gin.

cognac.definition: High quality grape brandy distilled in the Cognac district of France.
cognac.exampleUsage: The trainee asks what evidence supports the Cognac designation.

mezcal.definition: A Mexican distilled alcoholic spirit made from agave under the relevant product rules.
mezcal.exampleUsage: The product description identifies mezcal as an agave spirit.

triple-sec.definition: An orange-flavored liqueur category used in some mixed drinks.

amaretto.exampleUsage: The menu description notes the amaretto’s almond-like flavor.
amaretto.definition: An almond-flavored liqueur that may use almonds or other flavoring sources.

kahl-a.definition: A brand of coffee-flavored alcoholic liqueur.
kahl-a.exampleUsage: The stock list records Kahlúa separately from the other coffee-flavored products.

baileys.definition: A brand of cream liqueur made with Irish whiskey.
baileys.exampleUsage: The trainee checks the Baileys product information for ingredients and allergens.

grand-marnier.definition: A French liqueur made with orange flavoring.

chartreuse.definition: A brand of herbal liqueur produced in green and yellow varieties.
chartreuse.exampleUsage: The stock list distinguishes green Chartreuse from yellow Chartreuse.

campari.definition: A brand of bitter red alcoholic aperitif flavored with herbs and fruit ingredients.
campari.exampleUsage: The catalogue lists Campari as a branded bitter aperitif.

aperol.definition: A brand of orange-colored alcoholic aperitif with a bitter-sweet flavor profile.
aperol.exampleUsage: The buyer checks the information for the Aperol product rather than relying on its color.

drambuie.exampleUsage: The product sheet identifies Drambuie as a Scotch-whisky liqueur.

cointreau.definition: Cointreau is a French orange liqueur made by the Rémy Cointreau company.
cointreau.exampleUsage: The inventory lists Cointreau among the branded orange liqueurs.

tonic-water.definition: A carbonated drink with a bitter quinine flavor, often sweetened.

soda-water.definition: Carbonated water containing dissolved carbon dioxide, sometimes with added minerals.
soda-water.exampleUsage: The display includes soda water among common non-alcoholic mixers.

ginger-beer.definition: A ginger-flavored drink whose alcohol content varies; many commercial versions are nonalcoholic.
ginger-beer.exampleUsage: The guest asks whether this ginger beer contains alcohol.

cola.definition: A sweet carbonated soft drink with a characteristic cola flavor.

cranberry-juice.definition: A tart fruit drink made from cranberries, often diluted or sweetened.
cranberry-juice.exampleUsage: The refrigerator contained bottles of cranberry juice.

lime-juice.definition: Juice generally obtained by squeezing fresh limes.

simple-syrup.definition: A liquid mixture made from dissolved sugar and water, used as a sweetener in food and drinks.
simple-syrup.exampleUsage: The ingredient sheet identifies simple syrup as dissolved sugar in water.

grenadine.definition: Thin syrup made from pomegranate juice.
grenadine.exampleUsage: The trainee checks which ingredients are declared for this grenadine.

bitters.definition: Alcoholic liquor flavored with bitter herbs and roots.
bitters.exampleUsage: The guest asks whether the selected bitters contain alcohol.

lemon-twist.definition: A narrow strip of lemon peel used to garnish and flavor a drink.

lime-wedge.definition: A wedge-shaped piece cut from a lime fruit.
lime-wedge.exampleUsage: A lime wedge was used as a decorative garnish in the display.

orange-peel.definition: The outer covering of an orange, including its colored outer layer and pale pith.

cherry.definition: A small round fruit with a stone at its center, used as food or garnish.

olive.definition: Small ovoid fruit of the European olive tree.

mint-sprig.definition: A small stem of mint with several leaves attached.
mint-sprig.exampleUsage: A mint sprig was placed beside the sample glass for decoration.

cinnamon-stick.definition: A rolled piece of dried cinnamon bark used to add flavor or aroma to food and drinks.
cinnamon-stick.exampleUsage: A cinnamon stick added a warm aroma to the display.

salt-rim.definition: A ring of salt crystals attached around the edge of a glass.
salt-rim.exampleUsage: The ingredient record specifies a salt rim rather than a sugar rim.

sugar-rim.definition: A ring of sugar crystals attached around the edge of a glass.
sugar-rim.exampleUsage: The display showed a glass with a sugar rim.

cocktail-umbrella.definition: A tiny decorative paper umbrella used as a garnish in some drinks.
cocktail-umbrella.exampleUsage: The themed display included a colorful cocktail umbrella.
